title: Filing Relief for Natural Disasters Act
official_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify the rules for postponing certain deadlines by reason of disaster.
likelihoodReason: Became Public Law 119-29 on July 24, 2025. Passed the House on March 31, 2025 and the Senate on July 10, 2025.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended

summary: Lets the IRS postpone federal tax deadlines after a state-declared disaster (not just a federal one) at a governor's request, and doubles the automatic extension period from 60 to 120 days.
brief: Allows IRS tax-deadline postponements for state-declared disasters and extends the mandatory extension from 60 to 120 days.

top_lines.headline: State-Declared Disaster Tax Relief
subs: IRS may postpone tax deadlines for state-declared disasters
Triggered by written request of a Governor (or D.C. Mayor)
Mandatory extension period doubled from 60 to 120 days

items.main: Names the Act the “Filing Relief for Natural Disasters Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Modification of Rules for Postponing Certain Deadlines by Reason of Disaster

items.main: Authorizes the IRS to postpone federal tax deadlines for state-declared disasters and lengthens the mandatory extension period.
items.detail: Adds subsection (c) to Section 7508A of the Internal Revenue Code: on the written request of a Governor (or the Mayor of D.C.), after consulting FEMA, the IRS may apply its disaster-postponement rules to a 'qualified State declared disaster' (natural catastrophes, or any fire, flood, or explosion of sufficient severity). 'State' includes D.C., Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands. The mandatory extension period is increased from 60 days to 120 days. The changes apply to declarations made after enactment.

gaps: The bill lets governors request federal tax postponements but does not require the IRS to grant a request.
It covers state-declared disasters but does not otherwise change the rules for federally declared disasters beyond the longer extension period.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Kustoff
featured_quotes.text: This bill, the Filing Relief for Natural Disasters Act, H.R. 517, is a bipartisan bill and a commonsense bill. It  will provide relief to Americans who have been impacted by natural disasters and emergencies. Just about every Member of this body at some point has seen their State, their district, or their constituents impacted by a natural disaster or an emergency. Mr. Speaker, just last month, Obion County, which is in my district in Tennessee, was devastated by severe flooding following a levee failure.

added: IRS authority to postpone federal tax deadlines for state-declared disasters on a Governor's request (new Section 7508A(c))
modified: Mandatory disaster extension period increased from 60 days to 120 days (Section 7508A(e))

added: State-declared disaster postponements now require the Secretary to consult the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency before acting on a Governor's request
modified: On a state-declared disaster, the Secretary now applies the rules of subsections (a) and (b) — not just subsection (a) — to the qualified disaster
